The only state transition described is the one that occurs on the positive edge of `clk`: when `reset` is high at that edge, every flip-flop is loaded with zero; otherwise each flip-flop captures its corresponding `d` bit. Because the reset is synchronous, it has no effect between edges. A high `reset` that appears after an edge and is still high at the next edge affects only that next edge. Likewise, a `reset` pulse that rises and falls entirely between two positive edges is not part of the specified behavior at all. The output `q` is the eight-bit state of the flip-flops, and the specification says nothing about intermediate combinational paths, so the checker should treat `q` as changing only as a consequence of a sampled positive edge.

Power-up behavior is deliberately unspecified. The public description gives no initial value for the flip-flops, no power-on-reset sequence, and no guarantee that `q` is zero before the first clock edge. A checker therefore cannot assert a particular value of `q` before the design has been initialized by a defined event.
